clue.text: Pay the little twister!

definitions.meaning: in British slang a person's wages or salary can be called their ...
a small metal fastener driven home by twisting

explanation.definitionFit: Wages are slangily a screw in Britain, and a threaded fastener turned by a screwdriver is a little twister.

clue.text: Heavy dog possibly kept in a beastly home

indicators.note: kept in says the reworked letters are held inside the home that follows

parts.note: a sty is a home for pigs, a beast's dwelling

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word dog may come out in another order

explanation.surface: A heavy dog shut up in an animal pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy' looks like a description of the dog; it is the definition, as in stodgy food. 'possibly' marks the anagram and 'kept in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is dense and filling, so heavy in the sense of lying heavily on the stomach.

clue.text: Overwhelmed by accomplishment indeed!

indicators.note: the word indeed is split as in plus deed, so in tells us the feat goes inside

parts.note: the second half of indeed taken as written
a feat is a notable accomplishment

explanation.surface: Beaten by a remarkable achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split 'indeed' as 'in deed', so 'in' becomes the container signal; 'by' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten or bested is to be overwhelmed by an opponent.

clue.text: Feeling far from well in the main

definitions.text: Feeling far from well in the main

parts.words: Feeling far from well in the main
parts.note: the main is the open sea, so this describes a sailor's queasiness on board ship

explanation.surface: Someone feeling broadly unwell for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly', but here it means out on the main, the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by a ship's rolling motion is the queasy feeling of a voyager on the ocean.

clue.text: Get rid of listening device hidden in cuff

indicators.note: hidden in says the device is tucked inside the blow that follows

parts.note: a cuff is a blow with the hand, a clout
the ear is the organ we listen with

explanation.surface: Removing a bug concealed in a shirt cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' and 'cuff' paint a spy's bug in a sleeve; in fact cuff is a blow, CLOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out is a phrasal verb meaning to empty a place of unwanted things, to dispose of them.

clue.text: Cheat kind rival

parts.note: to con is to swindle or cheat
tender means gentle and kind

explanation.surface: A swindler being nice to a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor for a title or prize is a rival to the others in the race.

clue.text: Car tested, found faulty, and broken up

indicators.note: a test that finds faults suggests the letters of the two words are out of order

explanation.surface: A car fails its test and is wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dispersed into pieces spread here and there has been broken up.

clue.text: A sailing boat for backwaters

indicators.note: the first part of the word backwaters tells us to read what follows from end to start

parts.note: pools are bodies of still water

explanation.surface: A yacht suited to quiet stretches of river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwaters' is read as 'back waters': waters are POOLS, which read back give the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rig is a type of small boat.

clue.text: A friend made much of

indicators.note: made here means the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Someone whose pal is fussed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made much of' looks like 'pampered'; the indicator 'made' turns the letters of 'much' into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is an informal word for a close pal or mate.

clue.text: Unnecessary — might be lessened

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Something superfluous that could well be reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not required at all is uncalled-for, a synonym of unnecessary.

clue.text: Some of the arty-crafty types are so genial

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Craft-loving folk tend to be friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'types are so genial' as the definition, but only 'genial' defines the adjective; 'types are so' links. 'Some of' marks the run inside 'the arty-crafty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty manner is warm, cheerful and friendly, which is what genial means.

clue.text: This island appears backward to the old

indicators.note: appears backward tells us the phrase that follows is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written
ye is the old written form of the, as in ye olde shoppe

explanation.surface: An island that looks back-to-front in old-style lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears backward' reverses TO YE ('to the' in olde English) to give a small river island.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small river island, especially on the Thames.

clue.text: Enclosure is not at all simple

definitions.meaning: a fenced-in area holding buildings, as a prison or factory yard
made of several parts combined, as opposed to simple

explanation.surface: An enclosure that turns out to be complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A walled yard is a compound, and in grammar or chemistry a compound word or substance is complex, not simple.

clue.text: 27 accepting a good man's counsel

indicators.note: accepting says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is a guard, here taken as a barrier
St, short for saint, is a crossword stock for a good man

explanation.surface: A guard welcoming a decent man's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' is a cross-reference to the answer at 27 across, used here in its sense of a barrier; 'accepting' signals the insertion. A barrister is the British name for a courtroom lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain counsel is the courtroom advocate, a lawyer qualified to plead cases.

clue.text: The bounder in a jacket falls

indicators.note: in says the bounder sits inside the covering

parts.note: a case is a protective jacket or casing
a cad is an ungentlemanly bounder

explanation.surface: A rogue in a jacket takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' is a noun, waterfalls, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall, especially one tumbling in steps, is a cascade.

clue.text: Trade and make around two thousand

indicators.note: around says the verb is placed round the numerals

parts.note: to make someone do something is to coerce them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: Business that earns a couple of grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is the buying and selling of goods, the business of trading.

clue.text: Caught the second involved in a racket

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone seized for their part in a criminal scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a criminal scheme but means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud clashing din of hard objects banging together is a racket.

clue.text: City person putting money on acted right

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra, as in the sign for sterling
taken as written
done is a past participle meaning acted or performed

explanation.surface: A person betting cash on a correct performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the British capital is called after it; the City is also London's financial district.

clue.text: Those who rent are less troubled

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Tenants who are less bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessees, people holding property on a lease, are those who rent.

clue.text: Blooming fussy woman!

definitions.note: used as a noun, a flowering plant

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and fussy
Rose is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a fussy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild British oath, but it describes a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow spring flower blooms early, so the plant is a blooming thing.

clue.text: Duck benefit from gently-flowing water

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
use means benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: A duck profits from a slow stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a slow lowland river, a stream of gently moving water.

clue.text: A record, not English

parts.note: taken as written; the answer also running on into English is a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden word
E is the standard abbreviation for English; the forward run across these words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A recording that isn't English.
explanation.definitionFit: A written memorandum is a record of something.

clue.text: Carrying the can, got sent back outside

indicators.note: outside says the reversed word goes round the container
sent back says the word got is read from end to start

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Taking the blame, packed off home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' gives TOG, which 'outside' puts round TIN. 'Carrying the can' looks like 'taking the blame'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, often a weapon or a bag.

clue.text: In time he'll design a shed to snap together

indicators.note: In says the answer lies within the words design a shed

explanation.surface: A man builds a shed in his own time that clicks together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time he'll' is padding for the surface; the run sits across 'design a shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind or clash the teeth together, snapping them in anger.

clue.text: Value a steamer — Oriental steamer

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
E stands for east, and Oriental means eastern
SS again, for steamship

explanation.surface: Pricing an Eastern steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to evaluate it, estimating its worth.

clue.text: Seeing a mug in acute discomfort

indicators.note: in says the vessel sits inside the pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
a pot is a drinking vessel like a mug

explanation.surface: A cup seen while in sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting means noticing or catching sight of, which is seeing.

clue.text: Guard for a malefactor

definitions.meaning: a barrier around a field or garden that protects it
a receiver who handles stolen goods for criminals

explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is a guard round property, and a receiver of stolen goods is criminal slang for a crook's middleman.

clue.text: Coloured head's lack of experience

parts.note: green is a colour
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A coloured headland that is naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green means being inexperienced or naive, so the quality is inexperience.
